newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen lower, Motorola warns on earnings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen lower, Motorola warns on earnings.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were expected to open lower on Wednesday, jolted by a warning from semiconductor and telecommunications equipment giant Motorola Inc that its third quarter earnings are likely to disappoint.

Analysts said the comment was likely to post an early challenge to stocks. Surprisingly weak earnings from Motorola in July helped trigger a sharp sell-off that hit technology stocks particularly hard.
However, analysts stopped short of calling for another round of widespread selling pressure based on this quarter's comments.

"It was Motorola that helped shake up the market in July but since then it appears that the market has already digested most of the problems," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities.

Helping to offset the warning were several factors, analysts said, including Motorola's underperformance during the broader market's late summer recovery, an indication that investors remained aware of the company's problems.
Continued strength in the dollar was also expected to offer some support, said analysts.
